analysis.title: Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (SPCX): Q3'26 Preview: Framing the AI Segment Operating Backdrop & Increasing Operating Estimates Ahead of Earnings
key_insights: GS reiterates Buy on SPCX and raises the 12-month price target from $220 to $230 (44.7% upside to $158.96, price as of 2 Oct 2026 close). The target is a sum-of-the-parts on 2029 segment estimates discounted 1.5 years at 12%.

GS raises AI segment revenue estimates to about $27.3bn in FY26, $90.4bn in FY27 and $146.7bn in FY28, driven by more available compute and higher monetization per GW. Total revenue estimates rise to $51.6bn (2026E), $127.5bn (2027E) and $205.6bn (2028E).

GS estimates about 1.8GW of compute by end of Q3'26, based on management's disclosure of about 1.0mm operational NVDA GPUs across COLOSSUS I and II as of late September. Management visibility supports a base case of about 2.3GW by YE26, with upside to about 2.7GW. GS models about 2.4GW.

GS forecasts terrestrial compute capacity of about 7.0GW by YE27 and about 10.6GW by YE28, adding about 3.5-4.5GW per year. Key variables are power and cooling, datacenter shells and server (GPU) supply. Management cites projects totaling 15-20GW of power capacity by the end of next year, with timing uncertain.

GS assumes compute buildout is 100% terrestrial through YE28, with orbital compute scaling from 2029 (about 5GW in 2029 and about 19GW total in 2030). Management aims to deploy first AI satellites next year, and Google's Project Suncatcher prototype launched on a Falcon 9.

Short-term (3-6 month) hosting deals are priced at about $40-50bn+/GW. The two newest SPCX deals are at the high end of the historical $30-50bn/GW range. Nebius cited $40-50bn/GW and CoreWeave about $40bn/GW for short-term deals.

Longer-term hosting deals price at a floor of about $20bn/GW. IREN's 3-year contracts are above $20bn/GW with talks at about $25bn/GW, and Nebius cites $20-25bn/GW. Five hosting deals have now been announced publicly.

GS estimates an AI segment annualized revenue run rate of about $62.7bn (about $95.7bn total company) by year-end. The hosting (IaaS) business is expected to generate about $40-45bn of annual revenue in FY2027-28, the primary driver of the raised estimates.

Duration risk: most hosting deals are cancellable on 90 days' notice by either side, so revenue recognition at current rates through 2029 expiry may be too bullish. GS cites growth in the 1P model and enterprise software (Cursor acquisition, Grok releases) and tight industry capacity as support for returns even if deals are cancelled.

Street AI Solutions & Infrastructure revenue (Visible Alpha) is about $69.8bn in 2027 and $131.8bn in 2028. After backing out hosting deals, this implies non-hosting compute monetizes at only about $8-13bn/GW, well below current industry rates.

If IaaS revenue goes to zero in 2028, Street estimates would require about $18bn/GW on reallocated compute, which GS calls reasonable to conservative. Assuming 75% of non-hosting compute is monetized externally at $20bn/GW implies about 31% upside to FY27 and 9% upside to FY28 consensus AI revenue.

GS estimates are above FactSet consensus: 3Q26E revenue $15.19bn vs $12.71bn (+19%), AI revenue $8.26bn vs $6.35bn (+30%), GAAP EBIT $4.67bn vs $2.30bn, GAAP EPS $0.43 vs $0.16. FY26 GAAP EPS is $1.30 vs consensus of $(0.05).

Starship Flight 14 on 9/28 was judged largely successful: Raptor re-ignition, first orbit for Starship, first deorbit burn and commercial deployment of Starlink V3 satellites. GS expects iterations to drive reusability and launch cadence.

SPCX plans a $100bn Starbase LA launch site on the Louisiana Gulf Coast, with construction starting in 2027 and first launch targeted 2029+. GS expects 10+ launch pads by 2029 and now models 1x launches per pad per day in 2031 (vs 2x prior).

SensorTower data: Starlink MAUs grew +21% YoY in the quarter, down from +63% in Q2. Starlink app download growth accelerated from 31% YoY in July to 59% in September. X app MAUs turned positive YoY for the first time in 18+ months, and Grok app users grew faster than X.

Capex and cash burn are large: GS models capex of $71.6bn (2026E) and $221.6bn (2027E), with free cash flow of -$29.5bn and -$136.1bn respectively, funded mainly by debt. Key risks include founder governance, related-party transactions, dilution, unproven orbital compute and Starship reusability.

market_movers.rationale: GS raised the price target from $220 to $230 on higher AI segment estimates tied to compute capacity and hosting-deal pricing. Upside to the $158.96 price is 44.7%.

trade_ideas.description: Long SPCX, Buy rating with 12-month price target of $230
trade_ideas.rationale: AI segment compute capacity and monetization estimates are conservative versus Street, with differentiated advantages across space launch, connectivity and AI.
trade_ideas.risk: Governance and founder concentration, related-party transactions, high capital intensity and dilution, unproven orbital compute, Starship reusability, and 90-day cancellable hosting deals.

risk_factors: Governance: majority voting power and execution risk concentrated in the Founder and CEO.
Related-party transactions with companies tied to the Founder and CEO (Terafab and Macrohard co-development with Tesla, Tesla asset purchases).
High capital intensity and cash burn requiring large future fund raises, assumed primarily through debt.
Potential equity dilution from stock grants, management performance awards or equity raises.
Hosting deals are mostly 90-day cancellable by either side, creating revenue duration risk.
Orbital compute is unproven and depends on Starship reusability and rapid launch cadence.
Competition from other frontier AI models and from other launch and broadband providers.
Supply chain reliance on third-party chips (NVDA GPUs) and partners.
Higher than expected allocation of launches to internal use, reliance on government contracts, and fixed-price contract profitability.
Delays in regulatory approvals and licenses (FAA, satellite licenses).

tension_points.bull_case: Five hosting deals priced at $40-50bn/GW short term and about $20bn/GW or more long term, with industry capacity constraints pushing spot rates up. GS expects IaaS revenue of about $40-45bn a year in FY27-28.
tension_points.bear_case: Most hosting deals are 90-day cancellable by either side, so revenue at current rates through 2029 expiry may be overly bullish.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Cancellation of the hosting deals. GS notes that IaaS going to zero in 2028 would require about $18bn/GW on reallocated compute to meet Street estimates.
